title: Ship of Theseus
summary: Replace every part of something, one piece at a time. Is it still the same thing?
intro: A ship has every one of its planks replaced over years of repair, one at a time, until none of the original wood remains. The same puzzle applies to living things — including you.

questions.prompt: The ship has had every plank replaced over 20 years, one at a time, always staying seaworthy. Is it the same ship?

options.label: Yes — it never stopped being the same ship
There's no fact of the matter — it's just a label we choose
No — it's a different ship made of different material

questions.prompt: Someone collects every discarded original plank and reassembles them in their original arrangement, unused, in a warehouse. Which one is the 'real' ship of Theseus — the one that's been sailing, or the reassembled original planks?

options.label: The one that's been sailing all along
Neither deserves the name more than the other
The one made of the original material

questions.prompt: Almost none of the atoms in your body are the ones you were born with — they've been fully replaced over time. How much does that matter to whether you're still 'you'?
questions.minLabel: Not at all — I'm defined by more than atoms
questions.maxLabel: It's central — physical continuity is what makes me me

questions.prompt: A teleporter destroys your body, scans it perfectly, and builds an identical copy elsewhere with all your memories and personality intact. Did you survive the trip?

options.label: No — that's a copy; I died

questions.prompt: Same teleporter, but this time it malfunctions: your original body isn't destroyed. Now there are two of you, both with equal claim to your memories and your life.

options.label: Neither is fully 'me' anymore — something changed for both
Only the original, undestroyed body is really me

questions.prompt: A brain scan uploads a perfect functional copy of your mind to a computer, thinking and remembering as 'you' — but your biological brain is destroyed in the process. How much would this feel like continuing to live, versus dying and being replaced?
